First of three 64-byte multicolour sprite slots selected for sprite 5 by the Broadway raster handler. The game cycles the pointer through 3, 4 and 5 in VIC bank 1; this slot begins at bank offset $00C0. Each slot contains 63 shape bytes and one trailing byte.
Second 64-byte slot in the sprite-5 animation at $851E. The frame capture and the game's joystick controls associate this sprite with the steerable fireball; this slot is pointer 4 in VIC bank 1.
Third 64-byte slot in the sprite-5 animation at $851E, selected by pointer 5 in VIC bank 1. The byte at $8529 is the immediate operand used to set the pointer and cycles through 3, 4 and 5.

First 128 eight-byte glyphs of the character set at $7000. In the captured Broadway frame, the VIC uses bank 1 and the raster handler at $8595 selects this character base with $D018 = $1D. The bytes match between entry and play snapshots.
Last 128 eight-byte glyphs of the character set at $7000, selected in the Broadway frame by $D018 = $1D. The bytes match between entry and play snapshots.

First 128 eight-byte glyphs of the character set at $7800. In the captured Broadway frame, the VIC uses bank 1 and the raster handler at $8718 selects this character base with $D018 = $1F. The bytes match between entry and play snapshots.
Last 128 eight-byte glyphs of the character set at $7800, selected in the Broadway frame by $D018 = $1F. The bytes match between entry and play snapshots.

Byte 5 of glyph $AF in the $7800 character set, followed by more glyph bytes. The video chip reads this RAM as character data when the Broadway frame selects that base; the byte's other uses need checking.

Byte 6 of glyph $CF in the $7800 character set, followed by more glyph bytes. The video chip reads this RAM as character data when the Broadway frame selects that base; the byte's other uses need checking.

Clear the border and background and initialize state bytes at $8018–$8026, $9C74, $9C81–$9C88 and $9C8C–$9C9E, $96F0–$9713 and $973B–$9740, with selected bytes set to 1 or other starting values. Set additional operands and state at $8420–$8422, $851F/$8524, $87F7/$87FB, $895D, $919C, $9C6A–$9C73 and $8309/$830C. Copy 1,000 screen bytes from $3C00–$3FE7 to $4400–$47E7, then overwrite six cells at $47AF and $47B2–$47B6. Copy offsets 1–63 from $4240 to $4180. Set $0288 to $44 and $D018 to $1F, call $8484, and fill ranges of colour RAM with $0B and $0D. Override 22 colours at $DB51 with $0A and the corresponding screen bytes at $4751 with $FD, five colours at $DBB2 with $07 and sixteen at $DBA0 with $01. Write $06 to $DD00 and call $AF11 and $840A before entering $8260.

Write $DF to CIA1 port A and test bit $02 of port B. If it is set, continue at $829F. If it is clear, set $8027 to 1, call $8291, wait for that bit to become set, call $8291, wait for it to become clear, call $8291, then wait for it to become set again. Clear $8027 and continue at $829F. The meaning of this keyboard sequence remains open.
Three times, save the byte at $801D and wait until it changes, then return. The keyboard gate at $8260 calls this between input transitions.
Save A, X and Y, inspect the stacked status, then jump through the vector at $0314. The status test has no branch here; a BIT instruction follows it before the indirect jump.

Set display and sprite colours and enable all eight multicolour sprites. After calling $C901, write the mutable immediate operands at $851F and $8524 to sprite 5's X and Y registers, and the operand at $8529 to its pointer. Increment $801B; on four, clear it and advance the pointer through 3, 4 and 5. Acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $856F at raster line $59.
Position sprite 6 at X $38, Y $5B, select pointer 0, acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $8595 at raster line $61.
Combine $801E with $10 for $D016, set background colours and $D018, acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $85C6 at raster line $6F.
Set sprites 6 and 7 to Y $70, set sprite 7 X to $50, select pointers 1 and 2, acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $85FB at raster line $84.
Select pointers $26 and $27 for sprites 6 and 7 and position them at ($30,$85) and ($48,$85). Acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $8637 at raster line $99.
Set sprites 6 and 7 to Y $9A and select pointers $28 and $29. Acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $866B at raster line $AE.
Set sprites 6 and 7 to Y $AF and select pointers $2A and $2B. Acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $86A0 at raster line $B2.

Set colours and Y positions for sprites 0-4, copy their X positions and high bits from $9C6A-$9C74 and select pointers $52, $55, $50, $0A and $0B. Acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $8718 at raster line $CA.
Increment $801D, configure the lower display band and sprite 0, then call the sound update at $E13A. Acknowledge the interrupt and schedule $84E2 at raster line 0.
If the column pointer in the operands at $87F7 and $87FB is $0AE0, jump to the success path at $C9D5. Otherwise decrement $801E; when it becomes negative, mask it to three bits and call $87F4.

Read one byte from each of twelve backdrop rows, starting at the pointer in the immediate operands at $87F7 and $87FB and adding $01E0 between rows. Write the bytes at $4517, $453F and the following screen positions, forty bytes apart.
Increment the 16-bit backdrop column pointer in the operands at $87F7 and $87FB, then continue into the screen-shift loop.
For each of forty column offsets, copy the next byte left across twelve consecutive screen rows starting at $44F0. After the loop, continue with the state updates at $8929.

Increment $8028 and, every twelve calls, clear it and increment $8029. When $8029 reaches three, set it to $FF, copy the low byte of the store operand at $895D into the store at $894F, write $8A through that modified store and increment $895D; otherwise use $8029 to choose a byte from $8962 for $47A1. Continue at $8965.

Scan the Q key, then read joystick port 2 into $8020. On every second call, a pressed fire button calls $8CB5; releasing fire clears $8C10 on that check. Each pressed direction independently calls its movement helper: $91DD up, $91EE down, $91FF left and $9210 right. The scan can instead branch to the quit path.

If the fire latch at $8C10 is already nonzero, return. Otherwise set it and check $96F0; a nonzero value sends control to the next candidate at $8D8E. For a zero value, call $9192 and $83FB, set $96F0, derive screen positions from the sprite coordinates at $851F/$8524 and the row table at $9221, and update screen and colour bytes. If the selected screen byte is $FB or $FE, clear $96F0 instead. The remaining candidates and their effects need separate tracing.
If the byte at $8524 is at least $32, subtract 3 from it. That byte is the immediate operand loaded at $8523 and written to sprite 5's Y register at $D00B.
If the byte at $8524 is below $B6, add 3 to it. That byte is the immediate operand loaded at $8523 and written to sprite 5's Y register at $D00B.
If the byte at $851F is at least $68, subtract 3 from it. That byte is the immediate operand loaded at $851E and written to sprite 5's X register at $D00A.
If the byte at $851F is below $FD, add 3 to it. That byte is the immediate operand loaded at $851E and written to sprite 5's X register at $D00A.

If both $9C8C and $9C8E equal 3, clear $9C99–$9C9B. If $9C99 is nonzero, continue at $9DE8. Otherwise set $9C99, $9C71, $9C73, $9C8C and $9C8E to 1; set $9C70/$9C72 to $60/$80 and the operands at $86F8/$86FD to $0A/$0B. Increment $9C9E. When it becomes 2, reset it and patch four address operands at $9E39, $9E94, $9EFA and $9F55 to $F000, $F200, $F080 and $F280; patch the associated high bytes at $9E56/$9E5A, $9EB1/$9EB5, $9F17/$9F1B and $9F72/$9F76 to the $F0–$F4 ranges. Otherwise patch the four addresses to $F400, $F600, $F480 and $F680 and their associated high bytes to the $F4–$F8 ranges. The gameplay meaning of the two address groups remains open.
If $9C8C is 1, call $9E05; otherwise call $9C9F. Then if $9C8E is 1, jump to $9EC6; otherwise jump to $9CD2. This is the update path selected by $9D05 once $9C99 is nonzero.

Select a direction using $9C9A. When it is zero, if the high byte $9C71 is zero and the low byte $9C70 is below $A0, set $9C9A to 1 and return; otherwise subtract 1 from the two-byte value at $9C70/$9C71. When $9C9A is nonzero, if the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $90, clear $9C99–$9C9B and return; otherwise add 1 to the pair. Either movement increments $9C9C. On every fourth increment reset that counter and copy 64 bytes through the patched source at $9E38 or $9E93 to $4280. Advance that source by $40, wrapping its high byte at the patched limits. In VIC bank 1, $4280 is sprite slot $0A. The object’s gameplay identity remains open.

Select a direction using $9C9B. When it is zero, if the high byte $9C73 is zero and the low byte $9C72 is below $A0, set $9C9B to 1 and return; otherwise subtract 1 from $9C72/$9C73. When $9C9B is nonzero, if the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $70, clear $9C99–$9C9B and return; otherwise add 1 to the pair. Either movement increments $9C9D. On every fourth increment reset that counter and copy 64 bytes through the patched source at $9EF9 or $9F54 to $42C0. Advance that source by $40, wrapping its high byte at the patched limits. In VIC bank 1, $42C0 is sprite slot $0B. The object’s gameplay identity remains open.

Copy the pointer at $B088/$B089,X into the three load operands at $A50D, $A533 and $A53A. Add 2 to the saved index at $B0A2,X and read the sequence byte. If it is $FF, examine $B0BC,X: 0 backs the index up by 2, 1 restarts at index 0, and any other value clears $B172,X and returns. Save the chosen index, read the pair of sequence bytes into $AFD2,X and $AFD3,X, and return. The layout at $A540 uses those two values to select sprite pointers and a layout variant.

For entry X, add $18 to the 16-bit value at $AF9E/$AF9F,X and write it to $B1C0/$B1C1,X. Add $28 to $AFB8,X and write $B1DA,X; copy $AFD2,X to $B1F4,X. If $B172,X is not 1, jump to $A645. Otherwise select $A579 for $AFD3,X=1, $A5E3 for 2, and return for any other value. The identities of the entries remain open.

Build three further positions from the selected entry. Add $30, $18 and $30 to the 16-bit base $AF9E/$AF9F,X and store them at $B1C2/$B1C3,X, $B1C4/$B1C5,X and $B1C6/$B1C7,X. Store $AFB8,X plus $28, $3D and $3D at $B1DC, $B1DE and $B1E0 indexed by X. Store $AFD2,X plus 1, 2 and 3 at $B1F6, $B1F8 and $B1FA indexed by X, then return.
Compute the same three position pairs and offsets as $A579. Store $AFD2,X plus 1 at $B1F6,X, but write fixed values $BC and $BD to $B1F8,X and $B1FA,X, then return.
Write $08 to each of $B1F6,X, $B1F8,X and $B1FA,X and return. The entry at $A540 takes this path when $B172,X is not 1.

Call $AD6B with X selecting an entry and Y indexing a lookup table. Treat the returned byte as a signed offset and add it to the 16-bit base at $B0D6/$B0D7 indexed by X; store the result at $AF9E/$AF9F indexed by X. Negative values are negated and subtracted.

Call $ADEE with X selecting an entry and Y indexing a lookup table. Treat the returned byte as a signed offset and subtract it from the 16-bit base at $B0F0/$B0F1 indexed by X; store the result at $AFB8/$AFB9 indexed by X. Negative values are negated and added.

Read the selector at $B03A,X and compare it against a series of constants. A match selects one of the tables at $2000–$31F7 and returns the byte indexed by Y; for selector $70 the table starts at $2CCF. If no value matches, return with the selector in A.

Read the selector at $B054,X and compare it against a series of constants. A match selects one of the tables at $2040–$3827 and returns the byte indexed by Y; for selector $38 the table starts at $32FF. If no value matches, return with the selector in A.

Write the low X bytes at $B1C0, $B1C2, $B1C4, $B1C6 and $B1C8 to sprites 0–4 and shift the low bits of the following high bytes into $D010. Shift zeroes for sprites 5–7, writing zero X positions for sprites 6 and 7. Write $B1DA, $B1DC, $B1DE, $B1E0 and $B1E2 to sprite Y positions 0–4, limiting each to $9D. Copy pointers $B1F4, $B1F6, $B1F8, $B1FA and $B1FC to $47F8–$47FC and write colour $0C to sprites 0–4. The raster handler calls this routine at $851B.

Use A to select a seven-byte record at $EB5C: one accumulator increment and three little-endian pointers. Clear the three $24-byte channel state blocks, initialize their pointers and counters from the selected record, clear SID registers, and enable the channel update flags.
Call the three-voice SID update at $E141, then call the separate routine at $E937 before returning.

If $E12E is nonzero, advance an eight-bit accumulator; on carry call $E3A3 for channel offsets $00, $24 and $48, then call $E43D for all three. For each enabled channel, write its stored frequency, pulse width, envelope and control values to the SID; finally write $E138 to $D418.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $E146. Initialization copies the selected record's first byte here; each enabled sound update adds it to the accumulator stored in the operand at $E14A.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E149 and the accumulator for the sound update. Initialization writes $FF here; the update stores each sum back. Carry from the addition controls whether it advances the three channel streams.

Read a two-byte sequence-table base from the stream into indexed voice state, then select the first pointer in that table.

Add the indexed voice's offset to its sequence-table base and advance the offset. If the selected two-byte pointer is zero, reset to the first table entry; load the selected pointer into the stream pointer and continue reading.
Copy three bytes from the sound stream into indexed voice state at $E0DF-$E0E1, advance the stream pointer by three, set $E0E2 to one, and continue reading commands.
Select $80 for the indexed voice's $E0E3 state, then continue reading commands. The following entry points select $40, $20 or $10 instead.
Clear two indexed voice state bytes, take the next stream byte into $E0D9, advance the pointer and continue reading commands.

Set bit $20 in the indexed voice's $E0C2 state, clear $E0C9 and $E0CA, and copy three stream bytes to $E0CE-$E0D0. The $E341 entry sets bit $04 instead. Both advance the pointer by three and continue reading.
Copy two stream bytes to the indexed voice's $E0DC and $E0DB state, copy the second to $E0DD, advance the pointer by two, and set $E0DE to $40.
Clear the indexed voice's $E0DE state and continue reading the stream.
Set the low two bits of the indexed voice's $E0C2 state and continue reading the stream.

Count down the indexed voice's delay. When it expires, read its byte stream: values below $80 set the next value and reload the delay, $80-$BF dispatch through the command table, and higher values change stream parameters before reading again. Save the advanced pointer when a value is accepted.

For the channel selected by X, read a byte from the stream addressed by $E0CB/$E0CC plus $E0CD. A byte with bit 7 set resets the stream offset to $FF and has that bit cleared. Add $E0D3, the global offset at $E464 and $E0E5; use the result to select a little-endian frequency from $E5C2. The continuation at $E464 applies the channel's optional frequency and pulse adjustments and stores the resulting SID values in its state block.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E463. Initialization clears it; a sound-stream command at $E2C7 replaces it. The same routine then adds the channel byte at $E0E5, looks up a two-byte frequency and applies enabled pitch and pulse-width adjustments before storing the channel's frequency at $E0D6/$E0D7 and pulse width at $E0D8/$E0D9.

The first 82 little-endian values in the sound driver's frequency lookup. The driver doubles its index and reads a pair at $E46C and $E471; the sampled story, Broadway and outcome selections read within this portion. The table's full extent remains open.
The high byte of the first frequency value; the little-endian pairs begin one byte earlier at $E5C2 and continue through $E665.
Fourteen low bytes of pointers selected by a sound command at $E3EF. The matching high bytes start at $E676.
Fourteen high bytes of pointers selected by a sound command at $E3F5. The matching low bytes start at $E668; the pointed-to data remains open.

Update the shared modulation state, then call each active voice's effect routine according to the three flags at $E12F-$E131.

Update the first voice's timed effect. When its remaining count reaches zero, clear its active flag and envelope registers and set its completion flag. Otherwise count down the effect, periodically reload its frequency and add or subtract its configured frequency step before writing SID voice 1.
Update the second voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 2.
Update the third voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 3.
Clear the four sound flags at $E12E–$E131, then clear SID registers $D400–$D417. The following entry at $EB34 performs only the register clear.
Shift the four-byte state at $EB58-$EB5B, feeding in a value derived from $EB58 and the incoming carry; return the new byte at $EB58.
